original_cut: 'Leaves of Grass makes Whitman; The Secret Book of Walt makes something out of the Whitman that Leaves of Grass made.' … 'Singular magnitude is not claimed for the book in the work.'
proposed_finding: The Secret Book of Walt takes Whitman's solution to death and makes it permanent. Leaves of Grass sets an I beneath the I and promises that the speaking I will be with the reader, and with all souls, at the moment of death, so that there is no death. Whitman makes the promise as poet and perhaps prophet, on the American substrate, and in the 1855 Preface names the condition under which liberty would at last be discharged from a place: martyrs forgotten, patriots laughed at, boys christened after tyrants and traitors, laws for informers and bloodmoney sweet to the people. When that condition is substantially fulfilled, the American substrate has collapsed and the promise has lost its vehicle. The book changes the vehicle: it makes the operation scripture, continuous with the prior tradition — The Secret Book of John carried sentence by sentence, Whitman set in the redeemer's place and in the line of incarnations, the last incarnation left only the power 'to say what had been said, except / with a little touch of power.' The claim stands in the work. The book is the most vulnerable of the claimant works and knows it: each incarnation is 'the same, but worse each time', it asks 'Will it be enough?', and the Demiurge it lampoons is a foil whose operations are the ones to which the book itself is most exposed.
